title: Patient Financial Assistance Program Award Discount: Points for the Household's Coverage
content:
An award discount on a patient invoice under the Patient Financial Assistance Program carries coverage points, read from the household's Insurance Coverage & Claims records. The coverage points are added to the discount percent of the award's tier, and the resulting award discount percent is applied once, as one percent.

## Decision table

| Household's Insurance Coverage & Claims records | Plan the invoice was adjudicated by | Coverage points |
|---|---|---|
| No coverage in active status on file | Not read | 10 |
| At least one coverage in active status | A plan not sponsored through an employer group: an individually bought or government plan, recorded on its coverage as not an employer plan | 5 |
| At least one coverage in active status | A plan sponsored through an employer group, of any group size | none |

**Rule in words.** A household with no active coverage on file adds 10 points. A household with an active coverage whose invoice was adjudicated by a plan not sponsored through an employer group, an individually bought or government plan, adds 5 points. Any other household adds no coverage points.

## Points of judgement

- The first row looks only at whether any coverage on file is in active status. Coverages that are pending verification, inactive or terminated are not active coverage.
- The second row looks at the coverage the invoice was adjudicated under (the coverage the invoice is billed against), and asks whether that plan was sponsored through an employer group.
- The points are a number of percentage points. **Illustration (hypothetical award):** at a tier whose discount percent is 50, a household with no active coverage on file carries an award discount percent of 60, applied as one percent; with 5 points it carries 55.
